label: Oil Production
source: Iraqi Cabinet / Bloomberg / Turkish Minute / AGBI July 2026
contestNote: Pre-crisis (Jan 2026): ~4.4M bpd. Hormuz blockade (Feb–June 2026) cut production to ~800K bpd at trough; recovery to ~1.5M bpd. Iraq cabinet approved (June 2) tripling Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline exports from 220K to 770K bpd target by late August 2026. Basra southern terminals severely constrained; full Hormuz normalization needed for full recovery. ~37M barrels in floating/onshore storage. The 1973 Iraq-Turkey Pipeline treaty governing Ceyhan exports expires July 27, 2026; Turkey rejected a like-for-like extension and both sides are negotiating an interim protocol to keep 200K+ bpd flowing while a successor deal is worked out, adding fresh uncertainty to the northern export route.
deltaNote: Hormuz blockade (US-Iran war, from Feb 2026) restricts southern export capacity. Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline ramp-up to 770K bpd underway (June 2026), now complicated by the ITP treaty's July 27 expiration. Basra-Haditha pipeline ($1.5B, construction May 2026) is 18–24 months from operational. KRG-Baghdad dispute over $110B gas contracts adds political risk to northern export route. PM Zaidi's July 13–14 Washington visit included a proposed US-Iraq energy fund built around 500K bpd of exports in return for electricity-sector support.

label: Annual Oil Export Revenue
source: Bloomberg / SOMO / IMF / AGBI / The National August 2026
contestNote: H1 2026 oil export earnings totaled ~$18.5B (AGBI), far below budget projections. Monthly revenue collapsed from ~$6.8B in February to ~$2.3B by June as the Hormuz blockade persisted. Iraq's debt has hit record highs as the government borrows to plug the gap (~ID13 trillion borrowed in the first five months of 2026). IMF/World Bank project the 2026 budget deficit could reach 8-11% of GDP. A one-year Kirkuk-Ceyhan transit deal (signed Aug 1, 750K bpd capacity, ~170K bpd actual flow) offers only partial relief; Baghdad separately sought special Hormuz transit arrangements from Iran during the Aug 19-21 Ghalibaf visit.
deltaNote: Iraq's $74B 2026 federal budget severely underfunded; public sector salaries remain the largest expenditure item. KRG's budget dispute with Baghdad persists. The Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline's underlying 1973 transit treaty expired July 27; the Aug 1 one-year interim deal keeps a reduced flow moving while a long-term successor is negotiated. Zaidi government faces simultaneous oil, KRG, and PMF disarmament crises heading into the September 30 deadline.
